principles.text: Trade both the first lower-timeframe reversal and the retest: if the 1-/5-min breakdown is missed, wait for a lower high / the anchored-VWAP retest or a retest of the declining 9/21 on the lower timeframe (TSLA short example). Keep stops tight, ideally below 1%.
Don't chase a missed trigger: ARM's 1-min breakdown happened in seconds and got too far from the 9 EMA; wait for a retest (anchored VWAP) instead.

Gaps are traded as support/resistance for pullbacks: in a downtrend (under the EMAs) a bounce back into a gap is a short-reversal level; in an uptrend a pullback into the gap below is potential support. Gaps do not have to fill.
For longs he wants market breadth to widen; with strength confined to software/cyber and Russell the weakest, he stays short-leaning.

Prefer the name with the shallower pullback, faster reclaim of the EMAs after a correction and smaller market cap (easier for a $15B stock to double than an $80B one) - SMTC over BE. Holding near the 50 EMA/anchored VWAP despite repeated push-downs is a sign of strength before a breakout.

His biggest drawdowns come right after equity peaks: not selling into strength, then overtrading/revenge trading and SIZING UP in the drawdown during choppy markets turns a 15% drawdown into 30%. Reduce the number of trades when the market or your trading is not good; wait for the fat pitch.
After several losses in one day (e.g. three in a row) a big winner that day is unlikely; losing streaks cluster in many trades over a short time. Taking a break of days/weeks resets the odds.
Every re-entry is treated as an independent trade, so each is judged fairly and equally.
